items.title: Divisibility by a nowhere-vanishing one-form
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, with boundary allowed, and let $\omega$ be a nowhere-vanishing smooth $1$-form on $M$. (i) If $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ satisfies $\alpha\wedge\omega=0$, then there is a unique $f\in C^\infty(M)$ with $\alpha=f\omega$. (ii) If $\theta\in\Omega^2(M)$ satisfies $\theta\wedge\omega=0$, then there is $\beta\in\Omega^1(M)$ with $\theta=\beta\wedge\omega$.
items.strategy: Pointwise evaluation gives the unique scalar in (i), with smooth local quotient where a coefficient of ω is nonzero. The coefficient identity in (ii) yields b_i=c_i,i0/ω_i0; antisymmetry verifies its sign. Local finiteness and the opened ACω partition-existence suppliers glue β, including boundary charts. Dimensions one and two are covered (the triple identity is vacuous where appropriate); empty M gives the unique empty function. Assigned consumers inherit ACω.

items.title: Restriction of a foliation transverse to the boundary
items.statement: Let $W$ be a smooth $(n+1)$-manifold with boundary and let $F$ be a codimension-one regular foliation of $W$ transverse to $\partial W$, i.e. $T_p(\partial W)+T_pF=T_pW$ for every $p\in\partial W$. Let $\omega$ be a nowhere-vanishing smooth defining $1$-form for $F$. Then: (i) $T_p(\partial W)\cap T_pF$ has dimension $n-1$ for every $p\in\partial W$, and these subspaces form a codimension-one regular foliation $F|_{\partial W}$ of the smooth $n$-manifold $\partial W$; (ii) the restriction $\omega|_{\partial W}$ is nowhere vanishing and defines $F|_{\partial W}$, with $\omega|_{\partial W}\wedge d(\omega|_{\partial W})=0$; (iii) every leaf of $F|_{\partial W}$ is a connected component of $L\cap\partial W$ for a leaf $L$ of $F$, with the intersection taken in the intrinsic leaf topology; (iv) if $F$ is transversely oriented by $\omega$, then $F|_{\partial W}$ is transversely oriented by $\omega|_{\partial W}$; (v) if $\eta$ is a $1$-form on $W$ with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, then the pullback of $\eta$ to $\partial W$ satisfies $d(\omega|_{\partial W})=(\eta|_{\partial W})\wedge(\omega|_{\partial W})$.
items.strategy: The sum of the boundary and leaf hyperplanes forces nonvanishing of i*ω and rank n−1. Boundary de Rham supplier gives wedge/d pullback; Frobenius supplies integrability. Local (y,t) coordinates identify intrinsic boundary components with restricted leaves, whose plaque classes partition those components into open sets. Coorientation and η restriction follow directly. Empty boundary is vacuous; a nonempty boundary excludes the impossible rank-negative case.

items.title: The winding number jumps by one across a regular planar arc
items.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an oriented closed piecewise-$C^1$ contour. Suppose that near $0$ it contains exactly one regular $C^1$ arc, traversed once with positive real tangent, and that the remaining contour is a compact set disjoint from $0$. Then for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the points $i\varepsilon$ and $-i\varepsilon$ avoid $\Gamma$ and $n(\Gamma,i\varepsilon)-n(\Gamma,-i\varepsilon)=1$.
items.strategy: Positive tangent can be affinely normalized and the real coordinate inverted after restricting to a symmetric image interval. The remainder is compact and separated from zero. The scaled graph integral tends to 2πi: bounded-u uniform convergence follows from f'(0)=0 and tails are bounded by C/(1+u²). ML controls the remainder and integer-valuedness turns convergence into equality. The orientation is positive and each arc is traversed once. All eight cited calculus/integral suppliers were opened; no dominated-convergence theorem or choice axiom is required.

items.title: The winding number is locally constant by an integral estimate
items.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a closed rectifiable contour of length $L$ and let $p_0$ lie off its trace. If $d>0$ satisfies $|z-p_0|\ge d$ for all $z\in\Gamma^*$ and $|p-p_0|<d/2$, then $\left|n(\Gamma,p)-n(\Gamma,p_0)\right|\le L|p-p_0|/(\pi d^2)$. In particular the winding number is locally constant on the complement of the trace.
items.strategy: The resolvent difference has numerator p−p0, and denominators bounded by d and d/2; ML gives L|p−p0|/(πd²). Compact parameter interval supplies positive d without choice. L=0 gives zero winding; for L>0 an integer difference of modulus <1 vanishes. Opened rectifiable-contour definition, integer theorem, ML and linearity match the claim. No substantive reader defect is reported.

items.title: C² inverses and scalar return roots
items.statement: Let $f$ be a $C^2$ map between open subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ with invertible derivative at a point. Its local inverse is $C^2$. If $g(s,t)$ is $C^2$ near $(s_0,t_0)$, $g(s_0,t_0)=0$ and $g_t(s_0,t_0)\neq0$, then there is a unique local $C^2$ root $t=T(s)$, with $T'=-g_s/g_t$ and $T''=-(g_{ss}+2g_{st}T'+g_{tt}(T')^2)/g_t$, evaluated at $(s,T(s))$. No choice axiom is used.
items.strategy: C1 inverse exists by the exact inverse theorem; cofactor/determinant differentiation makes its derivative C1. Apply this to (s,t)↦(s,g(s,t)) and restrict the inverse to (s,0); g_t stays nonzero locally. First and second root derivatives follow from the chain rule, with mixed partial equality for C2 functions. All domains are open and uniqueness is local; no choice axiom. No mathematical reader repair is reported for this item.

items.title: C¹ planar fields on a closed disk extend to a neighbourhood
items.statement: Let $X$ be a planar vector field $C^1$ up to the boundary of the closed unit disk $D$. It has a $C^1$ extension to an open neighborhood of $D$ whose value and first derivative agree with $X$ on $D$, including its boundary. This is a finite explicit extension, with no choice axiom.
items.strategy: The finite formula 3X((1−s)p)−2X((1−2s)p) samples inside the disk for 0<s<ε<1/2. Its tangential coefficients sum to 1 and radial coefficients −3+4 sum to 1 at s=0; continuity of DX gives matching derivatives. The segment estimate can be split at finitely many circle intersections, so matching limits prove C1 extension. Chain rule and mean value supplier hypotheses hold; no choice is used.

items.title: A C² saddle function has C¹ Morse coordinates
items.statement: Let $f$ be C² near $p\in\mathbb R^2$, with $df(p)=0$ and Hessian of signature $(1,1)$. There is a C¹ local diffeomorphism $(x,y)$ centered at $p$ for which $f-f(p)=xy$. The coordinate change is only asserted to be C¹.
items.strategy: Signature (1,1) supplies a positive axis and its negative H-orthogonal complement. The C1 implicit critical curve η exists since f_xx>0; b(y)=f(η(y),y) is C2 because b'=f_y there. Signed square roots have limits X_x=√(f_xx/2), X_y=f_xy/√(2f_xx), Y'=√(−b''/2), giving a C1 coordinate map with invertible derivative. X²−Y²=f−f(p), then (X+Y,X−Y) gives the required product. Only C1 coordinate regularity is asserted. No substantive reader defect is reported.

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ foliation on a second-countable smooth manifold, let $L$ be a leaf, and let $\tau:J\to Q$ be a vertical transverse interval in one foliation box. Then $\tau^{-1}(L)$ is at most countable. If a countable foliation- box atlas is supplied as part of the data, the countability conclusion uses no choice principle. Dense and nonembedded leaves are allowed.
items.strategy: ACω supplies a countable box atlas using the opened Lindelof statement. Adjoin the target and initial boxes. Open overlap components contain distinct least rational-box codes, each determining one successor plaque; least finite-word code injects reached plaques into N. Each target plaque has at most one vertical intersection. Zero-dimensional leaves are singletons, dense leaves use intrinsic plaque continuation. A supplied atlas avoids the only choice. F2 applies to positive leaf dimension, treated separately.

items.title: A finitely cornered regular plane curve separates without choice
items.statement: Let $c:S^1\to\mathbb R^2$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ topological embedding with finitely many corner parameters. Assume each smooth edge is regular up to its endpoints and the two incident one-sided tangent rays at each corner are distinct. Then $\mathbb R^2\setminus c(S^1)$ has exactly two connected components, one bounded and one unbounded, and each has boundary $c(S^1)$. No choice axiom is assumed.
items.strategy: Distinct incident rays exclude opposite directed velocities, so their sum defines a monotone graph coordinate at a corner. Finite compatible side patches around the embedded circle give connected left/right unions; the local winding jump distinguishes their components. Any complement component has nonempty boundary on the curve and meets a local side, hence equals its global component. Both boundaries are the curve and the compact-plane-complement supplier identifies the single unbounded component. All fourteen supplier statements match; only finite selections are made. No new defect found; reader changes concern audit worksheets.

items.title: C¹ Euclidean maximal flows, variational dependence and the finite C² upgrade
items.statement: Let U⊂R^n be open and Y:U→R^n be C¹. There is a unique maximal flow Φ on an open domain D⊂R×U containing {0}×U, and Φ is jointly C¹. Its time slices are local C¹ diffeomorphisms with inverse Φ_{−t}; $\partial_t\Phi=Y(\Phi)$ and $D_p\Phi$ is the unique solution V of $V′=DY(\Phi)V$, V(0)=I. Each regular point has a C¹ flow box. If Y is C², Φ and those flow boxes are C²; the second state variation W satisfies $W′=DY(\Phi)W+D²Y(\Phi)[Ve_i,Ve_j]$, W(0)=0. Individual trajectories of a C¹ field are C² in time. A trajectory remaining in a compact K⊂⊂U cannot have a finite maximal endpoint. These Euclidean conclusions use no full AC or DC.
items.strategy: Local compact cylinders satisfy boundedness/Lipschitz and the Picard inequalities. Volterra differences, uniform continuity of DY and both-time Gronwall give the stated C1 variational equation; differentiating that equation for C2 Y gives W, mixed and time derivatives. Inverse theorem yields flow boxes; uniqueness glues solutions and inverts time slices. Compact K gives a Lipschitz trajectory and a limit in closed K at a finite endpoint, allowing restart. All eleven suppliers match the local argument; maximal solutions are unique unions, so no DC selection is needed. No substantive reader defect was reported.

items.title: Finite cellulations of compact C² subsurfaces relative to an embedded graph
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a compact codimension-zero $C^2$ subsurface of a Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless $C^2$ surface $S$, with $C^2$ boundary. Let $G\subset\operatorname{Int}N$ be a finite embedded graph: its vertices are distinct points, each edge is a regular $C^2$ embedded arc up to its endpoints, and different edge interiors are disjoint and avoid the vertices. Closed regular edges may first be subdivided by inserting finitely many vertices. Then $N$ has a finite triangular cellulation containing $G\cup\partial N$ in its one-skeleton. Each closed triangle is an embedded topological disk, the prescribed graph and original boundary retain their regular $C^2$ arcs, and the cell maps induce a homeomorphism from a finite abstract simplicial complex onto $N$ after finite subdivision. Interior edges have two incident triangles and boundary edges one; vertex links are circles or intervals, respectively. A cell map is required to be a homeomorphism; the statement does not assert a differentiable straightening of an arbitrary prescribed graph at its vertices. This permits tangencies between prescribed edge germs. The empty $N$ or empty $G$ is allowed.
items.strategy: Finite chart disks may be chosen with boundaries transverse to prior finite arcs using 1→1 C2 Sard. Prescribed regular edge germs have monotone radius near vertices, giving tame cyclic stars despite tangencies. Disk boundaries confine complement components to planar charts; finite side sectors count them. Trimmed cores preserve slit-side multiplicity. Polygonalization via arc strips and radial vertex interpolation, then vertical slabs and finite fans, gives disk faces retaining prescribed edges. Incidence subdivision yields a genuine finite simplicial complex, with circular/interval links; compact-to-Hausdorff pasting gives its homeomorphism. Empty N uses the empty realization. Nine exact supplier interfaces are checked; no mathematical reader defect is alleged.

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $S$ be an oriented Hausdorff $C^2$ surface without boundary, possibly disconnected. Then: 1. Every compact subset $K\subset S$ lies in the interior of a compact finitely cellulated $C^2$ subsurface $N$. If $K$ is contained in one connected component of $S$, $N$ can be chosen connected. A specified finite embedded regular $C^2$ graph contained in $\operatorname{Int}N$ can be included in its one-skeleton. 2. Every connected closed compact subsurface has an oriented genus normal form: the sphere for $g=0$, or the polygon word $\prod_{i=1}^g a_i b_i a_i^{-1}b_i^{-1}$ for $g\ge1$, with $\chi=2-2g$. A connected compact subsurface with $b>0$ boundary circles has a free fundamental group; capping its boundaries defines genus $g$ and gives $\chi=2-2g-b$ and free rank $2g+b-1$. 3. The fundamental group of every connected component of $S$ is torsion-free. 4. Every regular embedded $C^2$ nullhomotopic circle $c$ bounds an embedded compact disk region in $S$. Here a disk region is a compact subsurface homeomorphic to the closed disk, with boundary exactly $c$; its inherited surface structure and boundary are $C^2$. It is unique unless the **connected component containing $c$** is a sphere; in that component the two complementary disk regions are the two possibilities. The normal forms in clause 2 are homeomorphism normal forms. No general differentiable smoothing theorem or arbitrary-surface triangulation-existence theorem is a premise of this item.
items.title: Finite surface normal forms, Jordan disks, and torsion control
items.strategy: Compact regular superlevel subsurfaces are constructed by finite chart bumps and Sard. Relative cellulation provides a finite graph spine for boundary surfaces and a polygon schema for closed ones. Orientation and interlaced-pair reductions produce genus; cyclic boundary words are nonempty unless the surface is a disk. Shortlex least coset representatives supply amalgam data without full AC; the opened factor-action and normal-form proofs inject the length-zero coefficient subgroup as well. Reduced alternating powers and factor torsion-freeness prove torsion control. A null simple circle separates by a cellular intersection cocycle; if both sides were nondisks the injected boundary subgroup would contradict its nullhomotopy. Disk-side uniqueness fails exactly in the containing sphere component. C1 collars suffice. Corrected literal tab escapes in the collar formula to c×(−δ,δ)→N. All twenty-two dependency interfaces and the needed normal-form proofs were checked; no classification or general triangulation theorem is silently imported.

items.title: Frobenius divisibility: d omega equals eta wedge omega
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$ with nowhere-vanishing defining $1$-form $\omega$, so $TF=\ker\omega$. Then $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$ and there exists a smooth $1$-form $\eta$ on $M$ with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$. If $\eta'$ is another such form, then $\eta'-\eta=f\omega$ for a unique $f\in C^\infty(M)$.
items.strategy: Frobenius gives ω∧dω=0 and degrees (1,2) commute with sign +1. Divisibility supplies η under ACω; difference of solutions is uniquely fω. The optional normalized field merely evaluates this already established f. All six dependency statements are checked; empty base and dimension-one forms are covered by the supplier.

items.title: Smooth foliated concordance of codimension-one foliations
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $F_0,F_1$ be transversely oriented codimension-one foliations of $M$ with defining forms $\omega_0,\omega_1$. A **smooth foliated concordance** from $F_0$ to $F_1$ is a codimension-one regular foliation $G$ of $W:=M\times[0,1]$, transverse to the two boundary slices $M\times\{0\}$ and $M\times\{1\}$, together with a nowhere-vanishing defining $1$-form $\omega$ for $G$ such that for $j=0,1$ the pullback $i_j^{*}\omega$ along $i_j(x):=(x,j)$ is a positive smooth multiple of $\omega_j$, and hence a defining form for $F_j$ with its prescribed coorientation. By [[lem-a-foliation-transverse-to-the-boundary-restricts-to-the-boundary]] each slice $M\times\{j\}$ carries the codimension-one foliation $G|_{M\times\{j\}}$ with defining form $i_j^{*}\omega$, so the requirement is exactly that these boundary foliations be $F_j$ with the prescribed co- orientations. The smooth structure on $M\times[0,1]$ is given explicitly by product charts: near $s=0$ use $(x,s)$ and near $s=1$ use $(x,1-s)$, with x a smooth chart of M. These are half-space charts with smooth product transitions, as required by [[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]].
items.strategy: Endpoint pullbacks are positive multiples of the specified forms, so the prescribed coorientations are preserved. The boundary restriction lemma supplies the endpoint foliations. Explicit half-space product charts handle both endpoints without applying the boundaryless product theorem to [0,1]. ACω is carried from the coorientation interface. The definition permits the trivial product concordance and does not identify an orientation reversal with the prescribed endpoint.

items.title: Curvature of an extending Bott connection lies in the transverse differential ideal
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a codimension-$q$ regular foliation of a smooth manifold $M$ with normal bundle $
u=TM/TF$, let $
abla^{B}$ be the Bott partial connection, and let $
abla$ be any connection on $
u$ extending it: $
abla_X=
abla^B_X$ for every $X\in\Gamma(TF)$. Let $I\subseteq\Omega^*(M)$ be the differential ideal generated by the $1$-forms that vanish on $TF$, i.e. the ideal locally generated by a coframe of the annihilator bundle of $TF$. Then, in a local frame of $
u$ that is parallel along the leaves for $
abla^B$, the curvature matrix entries of $
abla$ lie in $I$; consequently every coefficient of the curvature two-form $R^
abla\in\Omega^2(M;\mathrm{End}\,
u)$ lies in $I$, and $I^{q+1}=0$.
items.strategy: The explicit quotient frame π(∂yj) is Bott-parallel because [X,∂yj] is tangent. Its extending connection entries annihilate TF and lie in the ideal generated by dyj; dI⊂I follows from d²yj=0. The curvature structure equation puts both terms in I, and frame conjugation preserves this membership. q+1 factors repeat an annihilator generator, hence I^(q+1)=0, including q=0. An extension is supplied rather than constructed, so the AC-requiring connection-existence and Chern–Weil interfaces listed in deps are not invoked here. items.title: Relative generic position for characteristic disk maps
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $M$ be a smooth $3$-manifold, let $F$ be a cooriented codimension-one foliation of $M$ given by a $C^2$ foliated atlas ([[def-c1-regular-codimension-one-foliation-and-transverse-orientation]], read with two continuous derivatives), and let $\omega$ be a nowhere-vanishing $C^2$ defining $1$-form with $\ker\omega=TF$. Let $h:D^2\to M$ be a $C^2$ map and put $\beta:=h^*\omega$, the **characteristic covector** of $h$; its zero set $\operatorname{Sing}(\beta):=\{x\in D^2:\beta_x=0\}$ is the set of **characteristic singularities** of $h$. Write $C_+$ for any fixed closed collar of $\partial D^2$ in $D^2$ on which $\beta$ is already nowhere vanishing. (a) If $h|_{\partial D^2}$ is a closed transversal to $F$, that is, $\beta(\tau)\neq0$ at every point of $\partial D^2$ for the unit tangent $\tau$, then $\beta$ is nowhere vanishing on a collar of $\partial D^2$. (b) If $h(\partial D^2)$ lies in a single leaf, that is, $\beta(\tau)=0$ at every point of $\partial D^2$, then $h$ is homotopic relative to $\partial D^2$ to a $C^2$ map $h_1$ whose characteristic covector $h_1^*\omega$ is nowhere vanishing on a collar of $\partial D^2$; the homotopy may be chosen with tracks supported in an arbitrarily small collar of $\partial D^2$, and $h_1$ may be chosen arbitrarily $C^0$-close to $h$. items.title: Local generalized Poincare-Bendixson theorem for a precompact planar orbit
items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $Y:U\to\mathbb R^2$ be a $C^1$ vector field with flow $\Phi$. Let $\mathcal O^+(y)=\{\Phi_t(y):t\ge0\}$ be a positive orbit whose closure $K_0=\overline{\mathcal O^+(y)}$ is compact and satisfies $K_0\Subset U$. Put $K=\omega^+(y)=\bigcap_{T\ge0} \overline{\{\Phi_t(y):t\ge T\}}$, and assume $K$ contains only finitely many equilibria (zeros of $Y$). Then exactly one of the following forms holds: (i) $K$ is a singleton equilibrium; (ii) $K$ is one regular periodic orbit; (iii) $K$ is a nonempty finite set $E$ of equilibria together with at least one regular trajectory, and every regular point of $K$ lies on such a trajectory whose alpha- and omega-limit sets are points of $E$. The family of connecting trajectories in (iii) need not be finite. The conclusion uses no choice principle beyond the ambient Euclidean completeness.

items.title: A C1 planar gradient at a nondegenerate saddle has local stable and unstable curves
items.statement: Let $u$ be of class $C^2$ near a point $p$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb R^2$, and suppose $p$ is a **nondegenerate saddle** of $u$: $\nabla u(p)=0$ and $D^2u(p)$ is invertible with one positive and one negative eigenvalue. Then the $C^1$ field $X:=-\nabla u$ has a local **stable curve** $S$ and a local **unstable curve** $U$ through $p$: both are $C^1$ embedded curves containing $p$, the tangent line $T_pS$ is the positive eigenline of $D^2u(p)$ and $T_pU$ is its negative eigenline, and each of $S\setminus\{p\}$ and $U\setminus\{p\}$ consists of exactly two half-trajectories of $X$. There is a neighbourhood $V$ of $p$ such that every trajectory of $X$ that is defined and stays in $V$ for all $t\ge0$ lies on $S$, and every trajectory that is defined and stays in $V$ for all $t\le0$ lies on $U$. The convergence to $p$ along $S$ is exponentially fast as $t\to+\infty$ and the convergence along $U$ is exponentially fast as $t\to-\infty$: there are constants $\delta,C,\beta>0$ with $|\Phi_t(x)-p|\le Ce^{-\beta t}|x-p|$ for all $x\in S$ with $|x-p|<\delta$ and all $t\ge0$, and $|\Phi_t(x)-p|\le Ce^{\beta t}|x-p|$ for all $x\in U$ with $|x-p|<\delta$ and all $t\le0$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Godbillon-Vey class of a codimension-one foliation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$, let $\omega$ be a nowhere-vanishing defining $1$-form with $TF=\ker\omega$, and let $\eta$ be a smooth $1$-form with $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, whose existence is guaranteed by [[lem-frobenius-divisibility-gives-d-omega-equals-eta-wedge-omega]]. The **Godbillon-Vey class** of $F$ is $\mathrm{GV}(F):=[\eta\wedge d\eta]\in H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. It is well defined: $\eta\wedge d\eta$ is closed ([[lem-eta-wedge-d-eta-is-closed]]), and the class is unchanged by replacing $\eta$ by $\eta+f\omega$ ([[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-independent-of-the-choice-of-eta-up-to-an-exact-form]]) and by rescaling $\omega$ ([[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-invariant-under-rescaling-the-defining-form]]). Only the de Rham class over $\mathbb R$ is named; no integral refinement is defined on this page.
items.strategy: The definition uses smooth cooriented foliations under ACω, not an unproved finite-regularity extension. Existence of η, closure, auxiliary-form difference fω and rescaling invariance are supplied by the reviewed lemmas. Any two nowhere-zero defining forms have a smooth nonzero quotient by pointwise proportionality; log|g| and locally constant sign cover disconnected bases. The target is real degree-three de Rham cohomology, zero on the empty base, with no integral refinement. Nine dependency interfaces checked. Hurder–Langevin §3.1, printed p.10, equation (13) and Theorem 3.2, corroborate the construction with opposite η sign; source and manuscript forms yield the same η∧dη. Locator repair is metadata.

items.title: One-sided trivial-holonomy classes form a normal subgroup

The classes in $\pi_1(L,x)$ whose one-sided holonomy germ is the identity form a normal subgroup $N_j(L,x)\triangleleft\pi_1(L,x)$. Consequently the quotient $P_j(L,x)=\pi_1(L,x)/N_j(L,x)$ used to define ordinary one-sided limit cycles is a group.

Transport along the reversed loop is the homomorphism for alpha-first concatenation; its identity kernel agrees with the ordinary return kernel. Restriction to either half-transversal is a group homomorphism, whose kernel is normal and whose quotient is a group. items.title: A fixed leafwise cap gives a joint transverse product with exact collar data
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one regular foliation of a $3$-manifold $M$, let $W$ be a compact disk, and let $B:W\to L$ be a $C^2$ map into one leaf. Fix $x_*\in W$ and a $C^2$ transversal $\tau:(-\delta,\delta)\to M$ through $B(x_*)$. Plaque continuation of $\tau$ along $B\circ q$, for a path $q$ from $x_*$ to $x$, is independent of $q$ near $t=0$ because $B$ maps the simply connected disk into one leaf; write $T_x(t)$ for the endpoint in the transported transversal at $B(x)$. Then there are a uniform interval $J=(-r,r)$ and a jointly $C^2$ map $P:W\times J\to M$ with $P(x,0)=B(x)$, leaf-valued slices $P(\cdot,t)$ and transverse tracks $P(x,\cdot)$, such that $$dP^{-1}(TF)=TW=\ker(dt).$$ The uniform interval is constructed from the fixed cap before any actual section range is checked. Let $C\subseteq W$ be a prescribed collar region with a $C^2$ trace $f_C$ and its actual holonomy-trivialized section $t_C$, so that $f_C(x)=T_x(t_C(x))$ and each $f_C(x)$ is obtained from $B(x)$ by projection along the short flow segments of a fixed smooth positively transverse field $V$ near $B(W)$. If a smaller closed collar $C_0\subseteq C$ has compact section range $S=t_C(C_0)\Subset J$, choose an open interval $I$ with $S\Subset I\Subset J$. Then the restriction of $P$ to $W\times I$ satisfies $P(x,t_C(x))=f_C(x)$ pointwise on $C_0$ and on its interior. The boundary section may be nonzero. If $C$ is a collar of $\partial W$ and $t_C=0$ there, continuity gives such a $C_0$ as a special case.

The same fixed smooth positive field as the collar data is retained, or constructed by finite ambient-chart bumps when absent. Parameter reversal handles a negative τ. The reviewed root adapter gives joint C2 P, leaf slices and transverse tracks without requiring B to immerse. Section range S must be compactly contained in the already fixed J; then S⊂⊂I⊂⊂J yields exact collar equality on the same short V segments. Boundary-zero traces satisfy the range condition after shrinking. Thirteen supplier statements checked; no uniformity over infinitely many paths is inferred.

items.title: A flat transverse drift realizes the period-annulus frontier as an omega-limit set
items.statement: Let $X$ be a $C^1$ planar vector field on an open neighborhood of a compact disk $D$, and let $\Psi:S^1\times(0,1)\to A\subseteq\operatorname{int}D$ be a given $C^2$ leaf product as supplied by [[lem-c2-first-integral-period-annuli-have-c2-products]], with $X=a(s,\theta)\partial_\theta$ and a positive $C^1$ coefficient $a$. Assume the periodic curves $C_s=\Psi(S^1\times\{s\})$ bound nested Jordan domains $D_s$ and that $\Gamma=\partial\bigcup_{0<s<1}\operatorname{int}(D_s)$ is compact. Then there is a $C^1$ vector field $Y$ on a neighborhood of $D$ that equals $X$ on $\Gamma$ and off an outer subannulus and has a positive orbit $y$ with $\omega_Y^+(y)=\Gamma$. The construction uses no choice principle.

Explicit locally finite band functions define positive b with b≤(1−s)² and b/a≤(1−s)²/(1+L). Coefficients bounded by 2^−n d_n/M_n give V=o(dist to Γ) and DV→0; bounded tail supremum suffices and makes zero extension C1. Inner flat cutoff closes the other seam. A full phase turn changes ambient position by ≤2π(1−s_k)²; all phases recur and s→1 only at infinite time, so omega limit equals Γ. items.title: A separated characteristic disk has a minimal nonidentity simple cycle
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). A relative generic characteristic disk with closed transverse boundary and with distinct singular images in distinct ambient leaves ([[lem-characteristic-disk-singular-images-can-be-separated-into-distinct-leaves-rel-collar]]) has an inclusion-minimal simple regular or homoclinic characteristic cycle whose ambient holonomy germ is nonidentity ([[def-holonomy-representation-and-holonomy-group-of-a-leaf]]). Inward boundary and finitely many stable branches allow a nonclosed entering orbit; PB and distinct singular leaves reduce its limiting graph to one saddle and one/two lobes. Lipschitz arc boundaries have area zero and finite-measure continuity from above applies. Nested circles converge to one local arc at each regular point, giving a finite saddle graph or circle. Finite fixed target return words bind all approaching germs; identity at zero would contradict the nonidentity germs at t_n. items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, $L$ a leaf, and $x\in L$. For a chosen side $j$ of $L$, let $N_j(L,x)\triangleleft \pi_1(L,x)$ be the subgroup of classes whose one-sided normal- fence holonomy germ is the identity. A class $[\alpha]$ is a **limit cycle on side $j$** precisely when its image in $P_j(L,x)$ is nonidentity, equivalently its one-sided holonomy germ is nonidentity. The two groups $P_+(L,x)$ and $P_-(L,x)$ record ordinary right and left limit cycles.

Loops, repeated saddle vertices, shared edges, and parallel edges are allowed in the saddle graph and polycycles. When the disk boundary is transverse to $F$, the period annulus cannot meet it. items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation, $L$ a leaf, $x\in L$, and $j$ one of its two sides. For a based loop $f:S^1\to L$ whose class belongs to $N_j(L,x)$, and for a chosen sufficiently short normal fence on side $j$, define the representative-level predicate $Q_j(f)$ to hold when every sufficiently small positive normal displacement $f_\epsilon$ is null- homotopic in its leaf. At this stage $Q_j$ is a predicate on a specified loop and fence; no representative-independence is part of this definition. For clarity, a displacement is obtained by starting at a chosen positive point of the base transversal and continuing the loop plaque by plaque through a finite chart subdivision. Within each chart its transverse label is held fixed; the fence specifies the nearby endpoint in that plaque. Since $[f]\in N_j$, the return map is the identity on a sufficiently short interval on side j, so these displacements are closed loops. The quantifier means: there exists ε₀>0 such that every displacement with 0<ε<ε₀ is nullhomotopic in its own leaf. No uniform bound on the filling disks is part of the definition.

Then: (a) there is a sufficiently short one-field leaf-synchronized fence over $f$: a single smooth transverse field $V$ with flow $\varphi$ and a jointly $C^2$ family $F(u,t)=\varphi_{\tau(u,t)}(f(u))$, $\tau(u,0)=0$, $\tau_t>0$, whose levels are closed loops in single leaves; (b) compact leafwise sets are separated from short nonzero $V$-displacements: for every compact intrinsic set $K$ in a leaf contained in the domain of $V$ there is $\eta>0$ with $\varphi_s(K)\cap K=\emptyset$ for $0<|s|<\eta$; (c) every actual collision at every level uses an eligible pair in one fixed finite cyclic source word. Some eligible pairs may fail to collide at a particular height. When a cut gives closed subloops on its actual common interval, each retained subword has strictly smaller cut rank.

items.strategy: Finite ambient smooth-chart bumps construct one positive smooth transverse V. Compact intrinsic K inside its domain has a finite open diagonal neighborhood whose local plaque coordinates exclude nonzero short displacements; compact off-diagonal pairs give the remaining uniform time bound even for nonembedded leaves. items.title: A fibration over the circle has zero Godbillon-Vey class
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:M\to S^1$ be a smooth fibre bundle with connected fibre and let $F$ be the foliation of $M$ by the fibres of $q$. Then $F$ is a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation defined by the closed nowhere- vanishing $1$-form $\omega=q^{*}d\theta$, where $d\theta$ is the standard volume form on $S^1$, and consequently $\mathrm{GV}(F)=0$ in $H^3_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb R)$. In particular the fibre foliation of the mapping torus of a diffeomorphism of a closed surface has zero Godbillon-Vey class.
items.strategy: A bundle map is a submersion, so pulling back dθ gives a nonzero closed one-form. Its kernel integrates to connected fibre components, and the supplied connected fibre makes each fibre a leaf. The reviewed closed-form corollary gives zero GV; closed-surface mapping tori also have this pullback form. The mapping-torus supplier distinguishes its closed total space from a solid torus. items.title: Explicit Godbillon-Vey rescaling calculation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On $M=\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,z)$ let $\varphi=ze^{x^2/2}$, so that $\omega:=e^{-x^2/2}\,d\varphi=dz+xz\,dx$ is a nowhere-vanishing defining form and $F=\ker\omega$ is the regular codimension-one foliation by the surfaces $z=ce^{-x^2/2}$, $c\in\mathbb R$. The $1$-form $\eta=(xyz-x)\,dx+y\,dz$ satisfies $d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega$, and $d\eta=-xz\,dx\wedge dy-xy\,dx\wedge dz+dy\wedge dz\neq0$ with $\eta\wedge d\eta=-x\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, nonzero where $x\neq0$. For the rescaled defining form $\omega'=e^{y}\omega$, the form $\eta'=\eta+dy$ satisfies $d\omega'=\eta'\wedge\omega'$, $d\eta'=d\eta$, and $\eta'\wedge d\eta'=\eta\wedge d\eta+dy\wedge d\eta=\eta\wedge d\eta+d(y\,d\eta)=(xy-x)\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$; the difference is the exact form $d(y\,d\eta)$, the explicit instance of [[lem-godbillon-vey-form-is-invariant-under-rescaling-the-defining-form]] with $f=y$.
items.strategy: Recomputed dφ=e^(x²/2)ω, so the kernels agree and connected level graphs are the leaves. dω=x dz∧dx; η∧ω has cancellation of xyz terms with the stated sign. Differentiating η gives −xz dx∧dy−xy dx∧dz+dy∧dz, and wedge with η gives −x dx∧dy∧dz. Adding dy leaves dη unchanged and adds xy times the volume form, hence the rescaled form is (xy−x) times volume. Exact difference is d(y dη). The claim distinguishes a nonzero representative from its cohomology class. All five supplier interfaces, including the exact submersion connected-component statement, checked.
